children: Mazda Motor Corporation and Yazaki applied near-site, automation-focused wire harness production to the all-new MAZDA CX-5, cutting harness variants by approximately 80% and establishing a domestic supply system serving Mazda plants in Hiroshima and Yamaguchi.
Fewer variants can lower cost, simplify logistics, and reduce changeover time, aiding margins and supply reliability.
Localizing supply reduces lead times and disruption risk, improving production flexibility.
Process/product co-design can lift productivity and stabilize quality, supporting cost competitiveness.
Consolidated domestic supply boosts resilience to external shocks and demand swings.
Scaling beyond CX-5 could extend cost and resilience gains across lineup.

This is an early-stage operational shift aligning with Mazda’s supply-chain transformation goals, first applied to the new CX-5. A larger catalyst would require evidence of cost savings, margin impact, and deployment across additional high-volume models.
Based on the original press release from Mazda Motor Corporation distributed by Japan Corporate News.
